builder_plan.scenario: A self-hosted model uses more compute or memory than your workload can justify.
builder_plan.change: Check for a usable pruned checkpoint and runtime support before attempting model surgery.
builder_plan.baseline: The original unpruned model at the same precision, context, and load.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task quality, actual GPU memory, serving throughput, and preparation cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Prune, Don't Merge: Expert Compression of Mixture-of-Experts LLMs on Multilingual Production Tasks
summary: Replaces serving a full MoE model (or REAM-style expert merging) with a one-shot pruning pass that deletes the least salient experts, shrinking the model 25–50% so a 30B-class MoE fits tighter memory or cheaper serving tiers. Costs a single calibration pass plus some irreversible quality loss, and requires per-task validation because academic benchmarks understate production damage. Failure concentrates in the output contract: invalid JSON, broken layouts, runaway generation, repetition loops, and non-English outputs copying the prompt's English phrasing, so hard output gates must be re-validated after pruning.
rationale: Pruning is feasible on a single GPU via a one-shot calibration pass and directly addresses the 24 GB memory constraint, but the paper itself shows task-dependent format degradation that demands workload-specific validation before production adoption.
technique: REAP one-shot expert pruning for MoE LLMs

claims.statement: Replaces serving a full MoE model (or REAM-style expert merging) with a one-shot pruning pass that deletes the least salient experts, shrinking the model 25–50% so a 30B-class MoE fits tighter memory or cheaper serving tiers. Costs a single calibration pass plus some irreversible quality loss, and requires per-task validation because academic benchmarks understate production damage. Failure concentrates in the output contract: invalid JSON, broken layouts, runaway generation, repetition loops, and non-English outputs copying the prompt's English phrasing, so hard output gates must be re-validated after pruning.
At 25% experts removed, REAP retains 93.6% of Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507's generative quality versus 62.5% for REAM merging; REAP is significantly better in 16 of 20 production comparisons.
